channel.title: Tech-Economic Times
channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: EU to make addictive app features easier to switch off
item.description: The European Union will on Wednesday unveil new rules to crack down on influencer marketing, ban online features that trick Europeans and force platforms to give users the right to turn off "addictive" features.

item.title: OpenAI lets businesses claim ChatGPT profiles, adds AI agents for US ecommerce firms
item.description: OpenAI said on Tuesday it was launching "Businesses" in beta within ChatGPT, giving companies a way to claim and manage their profiles, update information and track how users engage

item.title: Anthropic brings Claude to Google Meet to tackle tasks live
item.description: Anthropic said on Tuesday it was bringing its Claude assistant to video conference platform Google Meet, as the company pushes to integrate AI deeper into everyday office work.

item.title: Nvidia scandal rocks tech world Web Summit
item.description: Allegations of Chinese spying on Nvidia dominated a top world tech conference on Tuesday, with some executives seeing potential opportunities in the turmoil at the US artificial intelligence chip giant. Chinese technology executives attending the summit highlighted emerging alternatives to Nvidia.

item.title: Google agrees to addition privacy protections in Spirit Airlines data sale
item.description: The agreement clears the way next week for approval of Google's $10 million deal to acquire Spirit data to train AI models. The union said it had won a more rigorous de-identification process than previously planned and added significant employee data will be excluded from the sale, including health and medical information.

item.title: AI training startup Mercor valued at $20 billion in latest funding round
item.description: Mercor said on Tuesday it had raised $750 million in a funding round that valued the AI training startup at $20 billion. The Series D round drew participation from Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, Nvidia and funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, among others.

item.title: Still possible chipmaker Nexperia could reunite with Chinese operations, CEO says
item.description: If the split becomes permanent, however, Nexperia's Chinese parent Wingtech Technology should be compensated, interim CEO Stefan Tilger said in an interview on the sidelines of the electronica 2026 conference in Munich.

item.title: Amazon's Ring launches flying camera, autonomous security robot
item.description: Amazon's Ring on Tuesday launched a new robotics business with two autonomous security products, a flying indoor camera for homes and a roving security robot designed for businesses, as the company expands beyond its established lineup of home-security devices.

item.title: TSMC to invest up to $1 billion in Anthropic, OpenAI
item.description: The company is positioning itself to benefit not only from supplying AI infrastructure, but also from owning stakes in some of the industry's most influential developers. TSMC's board approved on Tuesday an investment of up to $500 million to acquire shares in Anthropic at its initial public offering price, and an investment of up to $500 million to acquire preferred stock in OpenAI.

item.title: Russia's Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data lost after attacks
item.description: "The remaining 2.84% cannot be recovered due to critical damage to equipment and the absence of backups on the platform by customers," the company said in its statement.

item.title: Nvidia, Jensen Huang face shareholder lawsuit alleging investors were misled about spy affair
item.description: The complaint comes after President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating the affair, which Huang has acknowledged to and apologised for. Trump said Monday that Huang told him he had no idea the person could be involved in espionage.

item.title: Israeli AI security startup Bay raises $50 million
item.description: Bay says it addresses a primary barrier to AI adoption by "allowing autonomous agents to perform business-critical work safely while enterprises retain control and accountability at scale".

item.title: Alibaba chip unit T-Head files confidential Hong Kong IPO application
item.description: China's Alibaba Group said on Tuesday that its chip unit, T-Head, has confidentially filed a listing application with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange after receiving approval to proceed with a spin-off.

item.title: Cognizant commits over 25,000 professionals to Anthropic's Claude delivery
item.description: The group is focused on execution excellence, transformation and client success, with the scale to take AI from pilot to production across enterprises' core operations, the Nasdaq-listed IT company said.

item.title: Anthropic targets valuation of about $1 trillion in IPO
item.description: Anthropic has entered into agreements with partners AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC, who will purchase $26.0 billion of its Class N common stock in a private placement.

item.title: Microsoft presses President Trump to scuttle expected ban on Chinese data centre technology
item.description: Reuters reported in August that the Trump administration wants to ban US imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within data centers. The concern is that they could be used by Beijing to steal data, install malware or disrupt service at US data centers.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged spy aided $7.5 billion in China chip shipments: The Information
item.description: Alice Huang, along with her husband and sister, built a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, according to the report.

item.title: Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman tied to Nvidia's CEO?
item.description: Known also as Huang Le, the Chinese businesswoman held senior roles at a Shanghai investment firm before becoming the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, according to more than 30 publicly available financial records, corporate filings and company materials reviewed by Reuters.

item.title: Anthropic plans IPO live stream with Dario Amodei, JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon
item.description: The meeting is part of the marketing effort for Anthropic’s potentially record-breaking IPO. The offering is expected to formally begin marketing as soon as early Tuesday ahead of pricing and the Nasdaq debut of its shares before the US Thanksgiving holiday, Bloomberg has reported.

item.title: What we know - and what we don't - as Nvidia investigates an alleged spy plot involving its CEO
item.description: China's Foreign Ministry dismissed the spying allegations on Monday, saying they amount to a smear campaign.

item.title: Quantum could solve AI energy drain, says tech founder
item.description: Quantum computers could curb the vast energy demands of artificial intelligence data centres with their ability to run complex calculations, one of the tech's pioneers told AFP. Australian startup Diraq is conducting the first field test worldwide putting a small quantum computer based on a silicon chip in a commercial data centre in Sydney. Diraq's computer installed in Equinix's Sydney data centre has eight quantum bits, or qubits, on a silicon chip.

item.title: AI demand unlikely to be derailed by Nvidia CEO controversy: Taiwan supply chain executives
item.description: Global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to remain strong despite the controversy surrounding Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, with Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain sources expecting limited long-term impact on the industry, according to a news report by Focus Taiwan.

item.title: Australia to adopt 'mandatory' AI safeguards
item.description: Artificial intelligence companies will have to abide by new "mandatory" safeguards when operating in Australia, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday. With immense renewable energy potential and vast stretches of uninhabited land, Australia has billed itself as a prime location for the data centres needed to power artificial intelligence.

item.title: US sues Lyft, alleges discrimination against disabled riders
item.description: The US Justice Department sued Lyft on Monday, alleging the ride-hailing ​services provider discriminated against passengers with disabilities, including those who use service animals and mobility devices such as stowable wheelchairs.

item.title: Anthropic unveils new Fable, Mythos models as competition heats up ahead of IPO
item.description: Anthropic on Monday unveiled two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as the OpenAI rival looks to strengthen its position in the fast-growing AI market ahead of its planned IPO.

item.title: Google to introduce two variants of in-house chips: Bloomberg News
item.description: The search giant's shares were up more than 2% in premarket trading. Through last close, the stock has fallen 9% so far this year. Alphabet did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

item.title: Apple Intelligence AI service registers with Chinese regulator for use on tablets, laptops
item.description: The cyberspace regulator in China's Shanghai said on Monday that Apple's generative AI service, Apple Intelligence, has been registered for use on tablets and laptops in China.

item.title: Enterprise data intelligence platform SplashBI opens GCC in Hyderabad, to invest over $100 million
item.description: The company plans to invest over $100 million over the next five to seven years in infrastructure, technology and talent to scale the Hyderabad centre and strengthen its global product engineering and delivery capabilities, a release said.

item.title: Banks, investors grow wary of AI debt, spooked by market selloff
item.description: Some banks, which just a few weeks ago were lining up to fund AI deals, are now telling market participants they would be reluctant to finance additional deals even when they involve guarantees from the sector's marquee technology companies, according to several banking and credit sources.

item.title: Sarvam names Google Cloud India head Sashikumar Sreedharan as president & chief business officer
item.description: Sashikumar will additionally join Sarvam's board of directors. He will lead the company's business across enterprises and government, while expanding its engagement with digital-native companies, developers and partners.

item.title: China dismisses spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
item.description: Huang has acknowledged to the Nvidia board that he had been intimate with a business executive who US intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, according to The New York Times.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang, the scandal-hit AI visionary in a leather jacket
item.description: Chips made by US chip titan Nvidia push the boundaries of artificial intelligence, but its leader Jensen Huang is in the spotlight over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. That is an area of concern to US officials who believe he has been involved with the alleged spy, Alice Huang, who is linked to a Singapore-based data center company, according to the New York Times.

item.title: Explained: Why Nvidia shares dropped 4% in overnight trade and what analysts warn can trigger a bloodbath?
item.description: Nvidia shares dropped over 4% after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang. Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice, a Chinese national, raised security concerns following intelligence reports. Nvidia has initiated an investigation into these allegations, although the board believes no secrets were compromised. Analysts suggest the company's upcoming earnings report will be crucial for market sentiment. Concerns linger over Huang's position if further evidence of wrongdoing emerges.

item.title: Tech firms claw back some losses after midterms rout, eyes on Nvidia
item.description: Tech firms rose Monday to claw back some of last week's painful losses fuelled by AI regulation worries, though traders were keeping a wary eye on a probe into Nvidia boss Jensen Huang amid claims of an affair with a Chinese spy. The executive, Alice Huang -- also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen -- developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.

item.title: IT firms with lower capital requirements may gain as investors shift focus to AI monetisation: Report
item.description: Information technology (IT) companies capable of monetising enterprise adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) without making substantial capital investments could gain an advantage as investors increasingly differentiate between businesses funding AI infrastructure and those generating returns from its adoption, according to a report by Anand Rathi.

item.title: “No excuse for what I did”: Read Jensen Huang’s full letter to Nvidia staff on his affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: In a message to company employees released Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologized to both his family and company staff. "I was unfaithful to my wife," he said. "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

item.title: South Korea says Nvidia issues won't affect contracted GPU supplies
item.description: Vice Minister of Science and ICT Ryu Jemyung told a parliamentary budget committee that 10,000 GPUs funded under a 2025 supplementary budget had already arrived and were in use.

item.title: Amazon rolls out text-based shopping through Alexa
item.description: Amazon said the new text feature lets users research and compare products, track deals and price drops, and have Alexa for Shopping complete purchases on their behalf.

item.title: USDA to launch AI tool to check crop production data after errors
item.description: After the USDA discovered errors in its corn data from September, officials determined the AI tool would have flagged the problem and decided to use it on the crop production report due on November 10, USDA Under Secretary Scott Hutchins said in an interview.

item.title: Snapchat starts disabling friend-finder feature for UK children, regulator says
item.description: Ofcom said the change would make it harder for strangers to contact children on the image-sharing social media platform, one it considers among the largest and most popular online services used by children in Britain.

item.title: Google acquires Wyoming data center site from AI infrastructure firm Crusoe
item.description: Google has acquired Crusoe's data center site in southeast Wyoming, the AI infrastructure developer said on Friday, a day after the Alphabet unit announced a $17-billion investment in the project.

item.title: Spy targeting Nvidia CEO was alleged China intelligence service recruit: NYT
item.description: The Chinese businesswoman, with whom Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang had alleged ties, was recruited as a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security, The New York Times reported, citing a memo circulated among policymakers in the Trump administration.

item.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation: Report
item.description: OpenAI completed a substantial funding round, securing $11 billion to increase its valuation to $1.25 trillion. The funding was finalized after the company scaled back its initial plans for over $30 billion. Citing market conditions, OpenAI has encountered shifting investor sentiment toward AI investments and infrastructure costs. Additional funds, which may raise the total to $20 billion, are expected to close soon.

item.title: Vaishnaw puts onus on social media platforms to curb online harm, stops short of safe-harbour clarity
item.description: Vaishnaw said social media companies could no longer remain passive intermediaries as the digital ecosystem evolved and must take responsibility for the harmful consequences of content circulated through their platforms, including cyber fraud and so-called digital arrest scams.

item.title: Want only serious players, no place for frivolous applicants in Semicon 2.0: Vaishnaw to industry
item.description: On Friday, the government launched the web application portal for Semicon 2.0, which will initially receive applications related to three of the programme's six pillars: machines and materials, fabs, and packaging. Guidelines have so far been issued only for these three pillars, and the portal is now inviting applications for them. Other three areas pertain to design, R&D and talent.

item.title: Activists breach Microsoft data centre construction site as protests spread in Europe
item.description: Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday, according to the "Stop Dirty Data Centres" coalition, which is rallying environmental groups and digital rights campaigns behind calls to pause large-scale construction.

item.title: Meta pauses planned terms updates, keeps existing rules in place
item.description: Meta has paused planned updates to its Commercial Terms, Product Catalog Terms, Self-Serve Ad Terms and Ad Creative Generative AI Terms, meaning the changes will not take

item.title: Alphabet discloses $548 million worth of Qualcomm stake
item.description: Qualcomm earlier this week irked investors when it missed Wall Street expectations for quarterly smartphone chip sales due to weak demand, even though it forecast better-than-expected revenue for its nascent data-center segment.

item.title: Apple's predictive text restrictions include 'Dictator Trump' and 'Sleepy Joe,' researcher finds
item.description: Hundreds of millions of people worldwide use iPhones, so Apple's choices about which words its keyboard suggests could quietly shape how they communicate. Apple has not publicly disclosed the list, the researcher said.

item.title: ING puts $500 million of data center loans up for sale
item.description: This includes a $25 million loan tied to a large New Mexico data center that forms part of the Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure venture backed by OpenAI, SoftBank Group and Oracle, the report said.
